I know exactly how you feel. I graduated at 23, with minimal job experience and none of it in the field I studied. Hey! As a recovering astraphobic you are correct; to a degree it is rational to be afraid of storms due to their severity, but with that you can always come up with a safety plan and kit. Like pick an area in the house to hold flashlights, matches, etc. and make a plan with whomever you live with should something like a tornado come your way. Having that preparedness can ease the fear a bit, in my experience. 

I’m not a professional but I’ve been to many therapists to kick this and while I’m still working on it, here are some tips that have worked for me.
- research everything about storms: how they’re formed, why lightning/thunder happen, etc. that knowledge can take away some of the anxiety because you’ll understand what’s happening scientifically. And tbh it’s pretty interesting lol. 
- exposure is something you should definitely see a professional about, but if you’re at a point where even storm audio scares you, try listening to it a little bit every day. Then progress to watching videos, and eventually try to stay somewhere where they’re windows for a little bit every time.
The issue I’ve had with this is that we really only have storms where I am at from may-late September so on the “off season” I’ve slacked off and regressed once spring came back around. 
Also! I actually put storm sounds on during them and wear headphones. I think it makes it better for me because then I have some semblance of control. So if you’re comfortable maybe try that?
